titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Solomon’s Son and the Division of the Kingdom (ch. 70)
part: ch. 70 — Solomon’s Son and the Division of the Kingdom
about: Zadok anoints Solomon’s son, who rides the royal mule; Solomon dies and is carried to David’s tomb with great mourning. Israel asks him to lighten the work; the old counsellors say to yield, the young say to threaten, and he answers harshly. Israel throws off the house of David, casts lots at Samaria, and makes Jeroboam son of Nebat king, leaving Judah and Benjamin to Solomon’s son. The text sets this against the promise to David, fulfilled in Christ and, on earth, in Menelik of Ethiopia, and closes with a genealogy of Mary and Joseph.

sentences.t: ፸ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘነግሠ ፡ ሮብዓም ።
sentences.l: 70. Concerning who-reigned Rehoboam
sentences.i: Chapter 70: Concerning the Reign of Rehoboam
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ ‘concerning’ + ዘነግሠ, ዘ- ‘he who’ + the perfect 3ms of ነግሠ ‘reign’, so ‘concerning him who reigned, Rehoboam’. ሮብዓም is Rehoboam, Solomon’s son; the text below usually calls him ዮርብዓም (Jeroboam), see the note on the next unit. The number ፸ is 70, spoken ሰብዓ (säbʿa).

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ነሥኦ ፡ ሳዶቅ ፡ ካህን ፡ ወአንገሦ ፡ ወቀብኦ ፡ ወገብረ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ዘበሕጉ ፡ ወአንበረ ፡ ዕፀ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ደብተራ ፡ ወረከቦ ፡ በስመ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወአጽዐንዎ ፡ ዲበ ፡ በቅለ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ባሕ ፡ ሕያው ፡ አበ ፡ ነጋሢ ፤
sentences.l: And-then took-him Zadok priest and-made-king-him and-anointed-him and-did for-him what-by-his-law and-set wood upon tent and-found-him in-name-of his-father Solomon, and-they-mounted-him upon mule-of king and-they-said-to-him: Bah, living father-of king;
sentences.i: Then Zadok the priest took him, made him king, and anointed him, and did for him what the law required. He set wood on the tent, and found him in the name of his father Solomon; and they mounted him on the king’s mule and said to him, “Bah! May the father of the king live (?)!”
sentences.n: The verbs are mostly ወ- + 3ms perfect with an object suffix: ነሥኦ ‘took him’, ወአንገሦ ‘and made him king’ (causative of ነግሠ), ወቀብኦ ‘and anointed him’; ዘበሕጉ is ዘ- ‘that which’ + በ- ‘by’ + ሕግ ‘law’ + -ሁ, ‘what is by his law’. Zadok anoints the king as in 1 Kings 1:39; the mule (በቅል, here the construct before ንጉሥ) is the royal mule of 1 Kings 1:33, on which David had Solomon ride and on which Solomon’s son now rides. The son is not named here; the heading names him ሮብዓም (Rehoboam), but the story calls Solomon’s son ዮርብዓም or ኢዮርብዓም (Jeroboam), as in ch. 69, and the northern king of Ephraim bears the same name (see the notes below). አንበረ ዕፀ ዲበ ደብተራ ‘he set wood on the tent’ is obscure: ዕፀ may be ‘wood’ or a ritual object, ደብተራ ‘tent, tabernacle’ (?). ወረከቦ በስመ አቡሁ ሰሎሞን ‘and found him in the name of his father’ I take as ‘acknowledged him as his father’s successor’ (?). ባሕ is an exclamation or acclamation I cannot identify (?); ሕያው አበ ነጋሢ is read as a wish ‘may the king’s father live’ (?), with ነጋሢ ‘king’ (an agent noun of ነግሠ ‘reign’, ‘one who reigns’).

sentences.t: ወደምፀት ፡ ሀገር ፡ ወተነፍሐ ፡ ቀርን ።
sentences.l: and-resounded the-city and-was-blown horn.
sentences.i: The city rang out, and the horn was blown.
sentences.n: ወደምፀት ‘and it resounded’ (ደምፀ, from ደምፅ ‘voice, sound’; 3fs because ሀገር ‘city’ is feminine); ወተነፍሐ the passive (tä-stem) of ነፍሐ ‘blow’, with ቀርን ‘horn’ as subject. The echo of 1 Kings 1:39–40, where the horn is blown and the city resounds at Solomon’s anointing.

sentences.t: ወዘእንበለ ፡ ይግባእ ፡ ኀበ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ አዕረፈ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፤
sentences.l: And-before he-enter to his-father he-rested Solomon;
sentences.i: Before he went in to his father, Solomon died;
sentences.n: ወዘእንበለ ‘and before, without’ + the subjunctive ይግባእ ‘that he enter’; ‘rested’ (አዕረፈ) is the regular word for death. The subject of ይግባእ is the new king, who had not yet gone back in to Solomon when he died; the sentence could also be read with Solomon as subject of both verbs (?).

sentences.t: ወወሰክዎ ፡ ኀበ ፡ መቃብረ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወላሐውዎ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ዐቢየ ፡ ላሐ ፡ እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘተረክበ ፡ ዘከማሁ ፡ በጥበብ ፡ በውእቱ ፡ መዋዕል ፨
sentences.l: and-they-brought-him to the-tomb-of his-father David and-they-lamented for-Solomon great lamentation, for none was-found like-him in-wisdom in that days ፨
sentences.i: They brought him to the tomb of his father David and mourned for Solomon with a great mourning, for no one like him was found in wisdom in those days.
sentences.n: ወወሰክዎ ‘and they brought him’ (ወ- + ወሰከ, which the published parts read ‘add’; here ‘bring to, join to’ (?)) + -ዎ ‘him’; ኀበ መቃብረ ‘to the tomb of’, a construct before አቡሁ. ወላሐውዎ ለሰሎሞን ‘they lamented Solomon’ with ላሐ ‘lament’ as a cognate accusative, ዐቢየ ‘great’. እስመ አልቦ ዘተረክበ ዘከማሁ ‘for there is none who was found like him’; በውእቱ መዋዕል ‘in that day(s)’ with the plural noun. Compare 1 Kings 3:12 and 4:29–34.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅረ ፡ ኀለፈ ፡ ሰቡዐ ፡ መዋዕለ ፡ አንገፍዎ ፡ ላሐ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ለዮርብዓም ፤
sentences.l: And-after he-passed seven days they-made-cease-(?)-him lament-of his-father, for-Jeroboam;
sentences.i: After seven days had passed, they made Jeroboam leave off (?) the mourning for his father;
sentences.n: ወእምድኅረ ‘and after’; ኀለፈ ‘pass’ with ሰቡዐ መዋዕለ ‘seven days’, accusative of time. አንገፍዎ: the -ዎ ‘him’ is an object, with ላሐ አቡሁ ‘the lament of his father’ as a second object and ለዮርብዓም restating the first (as in ወአንገሥዎ ለኢዮርብዓም below): ‘they made him, Jeroboam, cease the mourning for his father’; the verb itself I cannot identify and take from the context (?). A reading ‘they ended the lament for his father (and went) to Jeroboam’ would leave the -ዎ unexplained (?). Seven days of mourning is the usual period (1 Samuel 31:13).

sentences.t: ወተጋብኡ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዮርብዓም ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ አቅልል ፡ ለነ ፡ ግብረ ፡ እስመ ፡ አቡከ ፡ አክበደ ፡ ለነ ፡ በሐጢበ ፡ ዕፅ ፡ ወበውቅረተ ፡ እብን ፡ ወበአቅሞ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ ለአርውጾ ፡ ዕፅ ፡ ቄድሮስ ።
sentences.l: And-assembled people-of Israel to Jeroboam and-they-said-to-him: Lighten for-us work, for your-father made-heavy for-us by-cutting-of wood and-by-heaping-of stone and-by-setting-up-of cart for-conveying wood cedar.
sentences.i: The people of Israel gathered to Jeroboam and said to him, “Lighten our work for us, for your father made it heavy on us with the cutting of wood, the heaping of stone, the setting up of carts for conveying cedar wood.”
sentences.n: ወተጋብኡ ‘they assembled’ (tä-stem of ጋብአ). The request follows 1 Kings 12:4, “lighten the hard service of your father.” አቅልል is the imperative of አቅለለ ‘make light’; the verbal nouns with በ- (‘by cutting’, ‘by heaping’) are constructs: ሐጢበ ዕፅ ‘cutting of wood’, ውቅረተ እብን ‘heaping of stone’. በአቅሞ ሰረገላ ‘by setting up a cart’ (አቅሞ is the infinitive of አቆመ). ለአርውጾ ዕፅ ቄድሮስ ‘for conveying cedar wood’ is uncertain; አርውጸ ‘make run, convey’ is a guess from the root (?). ቄድሮስ ‘cedar’ recalls the Lebanon cedars of Solomon’s building (1 Kings 5:6). ዮርብዓም here is Solomon’s son (Bezold’s Jeroboam, the Rehoboam of 1 Kings 12), as in ch. 69.

sentences.t: ወመከረ ፡ ምስለ ፡ መማክርት ፡ ወመላህቅት ፡ ዘቤተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ አውሥኦሙ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ እስመ ፡ አንተ ፡ ይእዜ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሕፃን ፡ ዘኢያጽንዐ ፡ ሐቌሁ ፡ ለሐዊር ፤
sentences.l: And-he-took-counsel with counsellors and-elders of house-of king and-they-said-to-him: Answer-them kindly, for you now are-like child who-not-has-made-firm his-loins for-walking;
sentences.i: He took counsel with the counsellors and elders of the king’s house, and they said to him, “Answer them kindly, for you are now like a child whose loins have not yet grown strong for walking;
sentences.n: ወመከረ ‘he took counsel’ (ምክር ‘counsel’); ምስለ ‘with’; መማክርት ‘counsellors’ and መላህቅት ‘elders’ are plurals, the second from ልሂቅ. አውሥኦሙ is the imperative ‘answer them’ (አውሥአ + -ሙ); ሠናየ ‘well, kindly’ as an adverbial accusative. ዘኢያጽንዐ ሐቌሁ ‘who has not made firm his loins’: the elders speak of his youth as a child unable to walk. Compare 1 Kings 12:6–7, where the old men advise him to serve the people.

sentences.t: ወይእዜሰ ፡ ተናገሮሙ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ወበሎሙ ፡ እገብር ፡ ለክሙ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ዘትፈቅዱ ፤
sentences.l: but-now speak-to-them kindly and-say-to-them: I-will-do for-you all what you-wish;
sentences.i: But now speak to them kindly and say to them, ‘I will do for you all that you wish’;
sentences.n: ወይእዜሰ ‘but now’ (ይእዜ + the contrastive -ሰ); ተናገሮሙ is the imperative ‘speak to them’; ወበሎሙ ‘and say to them’ (imperative of ይቤ, form በል + -ሙ). እገብር ‘I will do’ (1cs imperfect); ዘትፈቅዱ ‘what you (pl.) wish’.

sentences.t: ወእምከመ ፡ ጸንዐት ፡ እዴከ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ፡ ትገብር ፡ ሕዝበከ ፡ ዘፈቀድከ ።
sentences.l: and-if it-is-strong your-hand over-them you-will-do your-people what you-wished.
sentences.i: and when your hand is strong over them, you will do with your people whatever you wish.”
sentences.n: ወእምከመ ‘and when, if’; ጸንዐት is the perfect of ጸንዐ ‘be strong’, 3fs because እድ ‘hand’ is feminine. ሕዝበከ ‘your people’ is an accusative object; ዘፈቀድከ ‘which you wished’. The elders’ advice is to yield for now, to win them over, and command later.

sentences.t: ወአውፅኦሙ ፡ ለመላህቅቲሁ ፡ ወአብኦሙ ፡ ለዕደው ፡ ዕንቡዛን ፡ እለ ፡ ተሐፅኑ ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ ወመከረ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፡ ወነገሮሙ ፡ ዘለአኩ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወዘከመሂ ፡ አምከርዎ ፡ መላህቅተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ንጉሥ ።
sentences.l: And-he-sent-out them for-his-elders and-brought-in-them the-men youths who were-reared with-him and-took-counsel with-them and-told-them what they-sent to-him house-of Israel and-how-also they-counselled-him elders-of house-of king.
sentences.i: He sent his elders out and brought in the young men who had been brought up with him, took counsel with them, and told them what the house of Israel had sent to him and also how the elders of the king’s house had counselled him.
sentences.n: ወአውፅኦሙ ‘he sent them out’ (causative of ወጽአ), ወአብኦሙ ‘and brought them in’ (causative of ቦአ); ለመላህቅቲሁ ‘his elders’ with ለ- doubling the object. ዕንቡዛን ‘youths, tender young men’ (?); እለ ተሐፅኑ ‘who had been reared’, the passive of ሐፀነ ‘nurse, rear’, a rare verb (?). ዘለአኩ ሎቱ ‘what they sent to him’ (ዘ- relative) and ዘከመሂ ‘and how also’ (ዘከመ ‘how’ + -ሂ) introduce the two things reported. Compare 1 Kings 12:8, 10.

sentences.t: ወይቤልዎ ፡ እሙንቱ ፡ ዕንቡዛን ፡ አረጋዊ ፡ ይገብር ፡ ምክረ ፡ አእሩግ ፡ ወልሂቅ ፡ ይገብር ፡ ምክረ ፡ ልሂቃን ፡ ወርሡእሂ ፡ ይገብር ፡ ምክረ ፡ ርሡኣን ፡ ወወሬዛሰ ፡ ዘከማከ ፡ ይገብር ፡ ምክረ ፡ ወራዙት ፡ ዘከማሁ ፡ ወእሉኒ ፡ ርሡኣን ፡ ደክሙ ፡ ሐቌሆሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሕፃን ፡ ዘኢይክል ፡ ሐዊረ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-said-to-him those youths: An-old-man he-does counsel-of old-men, and-an-elder he-does counsel-of elders, and-an-aged-man-also he-does counsel-of aged-men, and-the-lad-indeed like-you he-does counsel-of lads like-him, and-these aged-men are-weary their-loins like child who-not able walking;
sentences.i: Those young men said to him, “An old man follows the counsel of old men, an elder the counsel of elders, and an aged man the counsel of the aged, but a lad like you follows the counsel of lads like himself; and these aged men, their loins are weary, like a child who cannot walk;
sentences.n: The proverb-like run is built on ይገብር ምክረ ‘he does the counsel of’ with a construct plural each time: አእሩግ (plural of አረጋዊ ‘old man’), ልሂቃን ‘elders’, ርሡኣን ‘the aged’, ወራዙት ‘lads’. Enclitics: -ሂ ‘also’ (ወርሡእሂ), -ሰ ‘indeed, as for’ (ወወሬዛሰ), -ኒ ‘also’ (ወእሉኒ). ዘከማከ ‘like you’ and ዘከማሁ ‘like him’ are ዘ- + ከማ + suffix. ደክሙ is the perfect of ደከመ ‘be weary’. The young men turn the elders’ own image of the child against them. ከመ ሕፃን ዘኢይክል ሐዊረ repeats the earlier words, with ሐዊረ the infinitive ‘walking’.

sentences.t: ወበዝንቱሰ ፡ ነገር ፡ ዘትብል ፡ መኑ ፡ የአቢ ፡ ትእዛዘ ፡ እግዚእነ ፡ ንጉሥ ፤
sentences.l: and-in-this-indeed word which you-say who refuses command-of our-lord king;
sentences.i: and in this matter you speak of, who will refuse the command of our lord the king?
sentences.n: ወበዝንቱሰ ‘and in this indeed’; ዘትብል ‘which you say’ (ትብል: 2ms imperfect of ይቤ). መኑ የአቢ ‘who refuses?’ (አበየ ‘refuse’, imperfect 3ms). ትእዛዘ is the construct (accusative) of ትእዛዝ ‘command’; እግዚእነ ‘our lord’. The lads say: no one will dare disobey the king.

sentences.t: ወቦ ፡ እምኔሆሙ ፡ ዘይሰርር ፡ በቅድመ ፡ ዮርብዓም ፡ ወቦእምኔሆሙ ፡ ዘይመልኅ ፡ ሰይፎ ፡ ወቦእምኔሆሙ ፡ ዘይቀልብ ፡ ረምሖ ፡ ወቦ ፡ ዘይእኅዝ ፡ ቀስቶ ፡ ወምጒንጳሁ ።
sentences.l: And-there-is among-them one-who he-speeds-ahead (?) before Jeroboam and-there-is among-them one-who he-draws his-sword and-there-is among-them one-who he-swings his-spear and-there-is who he-holds his-bow and-his-quiver.
sentences.i: Among them are some who run ahead of Jeroboam, some who draw the sword, some who swing the spear, and some who hold the bow and the quiver (?).”
sentences.n: ወቦ እምኔሆሙ ‘and there is among them’ (ቦ ‘there is’ + እምኔሆሙ ‘from them’), then ዘ- + an imperfect: ዘይሰርር ‘who speeds ahead’ (ሰረረ as ‘sped, flew’ in ch. 30–34, root and sense from context (?)), ዘይመልኅ ‘who draws’, ዘይቀልብ ‘who swings (?)’, ዘይእኅዝ ‘who holds’ (አኀዘ). ሰይፎ and ረምሖ are the accusatives ሰይፈ and ረምሐ + -ሁ ‘his’, the ä + hu contracting to -o: ‘his sword, his spear’. ምጒንጳሁ ‘his quiver’ is a guess from context (?). The lads reduce the matter to force: they are the king’s armed escort.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ፈጸሙ ፡ ተውኔቶሙ ፡ አምከርዎ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ እግዚእነ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ንሕነ ፡ ምስሌከ ፡ ወአንተ ፡ ምስሌነ ፤
sentences.l: And-when they-finished their-revelry (?) they-counselled-him and-they-said-to-him: Our-lord, while we with-you and-you with-us;
sentences.i: When they had finished their revelry (?), they counselled him and said to him, “Our lord, while we are with you and you are with us,
sentences.n: ወሶበ ‘and when’; ፈጸሙ ‘they finished’; ተውኔቶሙ is ተውኔት + -ሙ ‘their’; I keep the published parts’ ‘revelry’ (ch. 62–63) (?), here the youths’ carousing. አምከርዎ ‘they counselled him’ (causative-type አምከረ + -ዎ), እንዘ ‘while’ followed by a nominal clause: ንሕነ ምስሌከ ‘we with you’.

sentences.t: ወአቡከኒ ፡ በጥበብ ፡ ወሀበከ ፡ ኪያነ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ምሁራነ ፡ ፀብእ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ከመ ፡ ንልሀቅ ፡ ምስሌከ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ትጽናዕ ፡ መንግሥትከ ፡ እምድኅሬሁ ፤
sentences.l: and-your-father-also in-wisdom he-gave-you us sons-of skilled-ones-of war, Israel so-that we-grow-great with-you and-so-that it-be-strong your-kingdom after-him;
sentences.i: and your father, in his wisdom, gave us to you, the sons of Israel skilled in war, so that we might grow great with you, and your kingdom be made strong after him.
sentences.n: ወአቡከኒ ‘and your father also’ (-ኒ); ወሀበከ ኪያነ ‘he gave you us’, with ኪያነ the accusative pronoun. ደቂቀ ምሁራነ ፀብእ እስራኤል: ደቂቀ is the construct ‘sons of’, and I take እስራኤል as its genitive with ምሁራነ ፀብእ ‘skilled ones of war’ in apposition between them (?); ምሁራን is the plural of ምሁር ‘taught, skilled’ (ምሀረ ‘teach’), followed by ፀብእ ‘war’. ከመ ንልሀቅ ‘so that we grow great’ and ከመ ትጽናዕ ‘so that it be strong’ are subjunctives (ትጽናዕ, 3fs with subject መንግሥትከ, has a vowel pattern unlike ይጸንዕ below (?)); በጥበብ ‘in wisdom’ I take to mean Solomon’s wisdom in giving the king these men (?). እምድኅሬሁ ‘after him’ (እም + ድኅረ + -ሁ).

sentences.t: ወአንተሰ ፡ እግዚእነ ፡ ኢታርእዮሙ ፡ ገጸ ፡ ሕመቅ ፡ ለእሙንቱ ፡ ሕዝብ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያምስሉከ ፡ ድኩመ ፡ ወዘኢትክል ፡ ገቢረ ፡ ፀብእ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ፡ ወላዕለ ፡ ፀርከ ፡ ወእመሰ ፡ ርእዩ ፡ ለነ ፡ ገጸ ፡ ድካም ፡ በቃል ፡ ወበምግባር ፡ ንከውን ፡ ሕቁራነ ፡ እምኔሆሙ ፡ ወኢይሁቡነ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ወጋዳ ፡ ወኢገብረ ፡ ወኢጸባሕተ ፡ ወትማስን ፡ መንግሥትከ ፤
sentences.l: And-you-indeed our-lord do-not-show-them face-of weakness (?) to-those people lest-they-liken-you weak and-not-able doing war against-them and-against your-enemy, and-if-indeed they-see to-us face-of weariness in-word and-in-deed we-shall-be despised by-them and-they-will-not-give-us gift and-(?) and-not service (?) and-not morning-offering (?) and-it-will-perish your-kingdom;
sentences.i: As for you, our lord, do not show those people a weak (?) face, lest they take you to be feeble and unable to make war on them and on your enemy; for if they see a face of weariness in us, in word and in deed, we shall be despised by them, and they will give us no gift and no tribute (?), no service (?) and no morning offering (?), and your kingdom will perish;
sentences.n: ወአንተሰ ‘as for you’; ኢታርእዮሙ ‘do not show them’ (prohibitive with the causative አርአየ); ዘኢትክል ‘and (one) who is not able’ (ዘ- + ኢ- + 2ms imperfect of ይክል); ኢይሁቡነ ‘and let them not give us’ (ኢ- + 3mp jussive of ወሀበ + -ነ); ገጸ ሕመቅ ‘a face of weakness’, ሕመቅ unclear (?), read from the parallel ገጸ ድካም ‘a face of weariness’. ከመ ኢያምስሉከ ‘lest they liken you’ (አምሰለ ‘be like, think’), ድኩመ ‘weak’ (ድኩም). ወእመሰ ‘and if indeed’; ንከውን ሕቁራነ ‘we shall be despised’, ሕቁራን plural of ሕቁር. The tributes: አምኃ ‘gift’, ወጋዳ ‘and tribute’ (?), ገብረ, which I take as ግብር ‘work, service’ written with ገ- (ገብር is ‘servant’) (?), ጸባሕተ ‘morning offering’ (?), a guess from ጸባሕ ‘morning’. ወትማስን ‘and it will perish’ (ማሰነ ‘perish’). The lads argue that a king who looks weak costs his men their dues, and the king his kingdom.

sentences.t: አላ ፡ በሎሙ ፡ በጽኑዕ ፡ ቃል ፡ ወበገንሕ ፡ ተናገሮሙ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ትብል ፡ አቡየሰ ፡ ትቤልዎ ፡ በዕፅ ፡ ወበእብን ፡ ወአንሰ ፡ እቀንየክሙ ፡ በጋጋት ፡ ወበዐቃርብት ፡ እስመ ፡ እምግዝፈ ፡ አቡየ ፡ ይጸንዕ ፡ ቊጠጠ ፡ ዚአየ ፡ ወእምክሩ ፡ ለአቡየ ፡ ለዘወለደኒ ፡ የዐቢ ፡ ምክረ ፡ ዚአየ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘኣነትግ ፡ ለክሙ ፡ ግብረ ፡ ወገብጋበ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ዘኣፈደፍድ ፡ ለክሙ ፡ በኵሉ ፤
sentences.l: But say-to-them with-strong word and-with-harshness speak-to-them while you-say: My-father-indeed you-said-of-him by-wood and-by-stone, and-I-indeed I-will-subdue-you with-whips and-with-scorpions, for than-the-thickness-of my-father it-is-stronger my-little-finger and-than-the-counsel of-my-father who-begot-me is-greater my-counsel; there-is-not what I-will-remove for-you work and-(?) except what I-will-add for-you in-everything;
sentences.i: Rather, speak to them with a strong word and harshly, saying, ‘As for my father, you said of him that he burdened you with wood and stone, but I shall subdue (?) you with whips and scorpions. For my little finger is stronger than the thickness of my father, and my counsel is greater than the counsel of my father who begot me. I shall take nothing from your work and your burden (?); I shall only add to it for you in everything;
sentences.n: አላ ‘but’; በሎሙ ‘say to them’; በጽኑዕ ቃል ‘with a strong word’ and በገንሕ ‘with harshness’ (ገንሕ ‘harshness’ (?)). The speech is that of 1 Kings 12:10–11 (‘my little finger is thicker than my father’s loins… my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions’). አቡየሰ ትቤልዎ ‘as for my father, you said of him’: ትቤልዎ is 2mp ትቤሉ (the prefix form of ይቤ used as a perfect, as ትቤ in ch. 69) + ሎ ‘to, of him’ (as in ይቤልዎ ‘they said to him’), not an object -ዎ; በዕፅ ወበእብን has no verb, and ‘burdened you’ is supplied from the people’s complaint in unit 6. እቀንየክሙ ‘I will subdue you’: the prefix እ- is the plain G imperfect (a causative would be ኣቀንይ-), so either ቀነየ (‘serve’) is itself used transitively here or the form is irregular; the sense is from the context (?). ጋጋት ‘whips’ and ዐቃርብት ‘scorpions’ are plurals. ቊጠጠ ዚአየ ‘my little finger’ is uncertain (?). ግዝፈ ‘thickness, bulk’ + አብ. የዐቢ ‘is greater’; ወእምክሩ ለአቡየ ‘and than the counsel of my father’: እም- ‘than’ + ምክር + -ሁ ‘his’ anticipating the genitive ለአቡየ, with one ም written (?). ዘኣነትግ: ነትገ ‘remove, take away’ is uncertain (?); ገብጋብ ‘burden’ (?). ዘኣፈደፍድ ‘what I shall add’ (አፈድፈደ). Note the lads’ counsel is the very speech quoted by the historical Rehoboam.

sentences.t: ወለእመኒ ፡ ኢሰማዕክሙ ፡ ቃልየ ፡ ወኢገበርክሙ ፡ ትእዛዝየ ፡ እገብር ፡ እንስሳክሙ ፡ ሕብልያ ፡ ወደቂቅክሙ ፡ ይከውኑ ፡ ፄዋወለክሙኒ ፡ መጥባኅትየ ፡ ትበልዐክሙ ፡ ወእነሥእ ፡ አህጉሪክሙ ፡ ወአዕጻዲክሙ ፡ ወአትክልቲክሙ ፡ ወዐዘቃቲክሙ ፡ ወገራውሂክሙ ፡ ወአዕጻዳተ ፡ ወፍርክሙ ፤
sentences.l: and-if you-did-not-hear my-word and-did-not-do my-command I-will-make your-cattle tethered (?) and-your-children they-shall-be slaves, and-as-for-you my-knife (?) shall-devour-you, and-I-will-take your-cities and-your-enclosures and-your-gardens and-your-wells and-your-fields and-enclosures and-your-fruit (?);
sentences.i: But if you do not listen to my word and do not do my command, I shall make your cattle tethered, and your children shall become slaves; my knife (?) shall devour you, and I shall take your cities, your enclosures, your gardens, your wells, your fields, and enclosures and your fruit (?);
sentences.n: ወለእመኒ ‘and if’ (ለእመ + -ኒ); ኢሰማዕክሙ ‘you (pl.) did not hear’. እገብር እንስሳክሙ ሕብልያ: ሕብልያ is obscure; I take ‘bound, tethered’ (?), as of animals led off. ፄዋወለክሙኒ is one word in the source: ፄዋ ‘captives, slaves’ (as in ch. 60) + ወ- ‘and’ + ለክሙ ‘to you’ + -ኒ, ‘slaves; and as for you’; ይከውኑ ‘they will be’. መጥባኅትየ is መጥባሕት ‘knife’ (ch. 30 has the plural መጣብሕ) + -የ ‘my’, a feminine singular, hence the 3fs verb ትበልዐክሙ ‘it will devour you’ (በልዐ ‘swallow, devour’); the spelling with ኅ is irregular (?). The list of possessions is all with the suffix -ክሙ ‘your (pl.)’: አህጉር ‘cities’, አዕጻድ ‘enclosures, courts’, አትክልት ‘gardens’, ዐዘቃት ‘wells’ (?), ገራውህ ‘fields’, and ወአዕጻዳተ ወፍርክሙ ‘and enclosures and your fruit’ (ወ- + ፍር ‘fruit’ + -ክሙ; አዕጻዳተ has no suffix and I do not take it as a construct) (?).

sentences.t: ወለክቡራኒክሙ ፡ በእደ ፡ ሰናስለ ፡ ኀጺን ፡ ወለአብዕልቲክሙኒ ፡ ሲሳየ ፡ አግብርትየ ፡ ወአንስትያክሙኒ ፡ ሰርጐ ፡ ለቤተ ፡ ክቡራንየ ፤
sentences.l: and-for-your-honoured-ones with-hand-of chains-of iron, and-for-your-rich food-of my-servants, and-your-women a-marriage (?) for-the-house-of my-nobles;
sentences.i: and for your honoured men, chains of iron; for your rich, food for my servants; and your women shall be given in marriage (?) to the house of my nobles;
sentences.n: ወለክቡራኒክሙ ‘and as for your honoured men’ (ክቡር ‘honoured’, plural ክቡራን, with its linking vowel before -ክሙ; the ኒ here is not the enclitic ‘also’ that ends ወለአብዕልቲክሙኒ and ወአንስትያክሙኒ). በእደ ሰናስለ ኀጺን ‘in (the) hand of chains of iron’ (እደ, construct of እድ ‘hand’, singular), a construct chain, meaning ‘in iron chains’. ሲሳየ አግብርትየ ‘food of my servants’; አግብርት ‘servants’. ሰርጐ ለቤተ ክቡራንየ: the published parts read ሰርጐ as ‘adornment’ (ch. 13–16); here ‘wedding, giving in marriage’ is my reading of the stem (?), and the threat is that the women will be given to the nobles’ house (?); a harsher sense, ‘concubinage’, is possible (?).

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ ቃልየ ፡ ኢያፀርዓ ፡ ወኢያሐጽጻ ፡ ወኢይሜቊሳ ፡ ወኢያበጥላ ፡ ወእገብራ ፡ ፍጡነ ፡ ወእከትባ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: and-this my-word he-shall-not-annul (?) and-shall-not-diminish and-shall-not-(?) and-shall-not-void, and-I-will-do-it quickly and-I-will-write-it for-ever;
sentences.i: No one shall annul this word of mine, or diminish it, or mar it (?), or make it void; I shall carry it out quickly and write it down for ever;
sentences.n: ወዘንተ ቃልየ ‘and this my word’; ኢያፀርዓ ‘let him not annul it’ (?), ኢያሐጽጻ ‘let him not diminish it’ (አሐጽጸ), ኢይሜቊሳ ‘let him not … it’ (the verb unknown; ‘mar’ is a guess from መቈሰ ‘wound’) (?) and ኢያበጥላ ‘let him not void it’ (አበጠለ): all four are 3ms jussives with ኢ- (a 3mp would end in -ዋ before the object), and the object suffix -ኣ is feminine, ቃል ‘word’ being treated as feminine. ወእገብራ ፍጡነ ‘and I will do it quickly’; ወእከትባ ‘I will write it’ (ከተበ). The king says he will put the edict in writing.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ኵላ ፡ ዘይእቲ ፡ ምድር ፡ ተውህበት ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ለአበ ፡ አቡየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወለአቡየ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ እምድኅሬሁ ፡ ወሊተኒ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ አቡየ ፡ ወሀበኒ ፡ ከማሆሙ ፡ ወእቀንየክሙ ፡ አነኒ ፡ ከማሆሙ ፡ ወይእዜኒ ፡ ምክሩ ፡ ወተአዘዙ ፡ ሊተ ፨
sentences.l: for all that this land was-given kingdom to-the-father-of my-father David and-to-my-father Solomon after-him, and-to-me-also after my-father he-gave like-them, and-I-will-subdue-you I-also like-them; and-now-also take-counsel and-obey me ፨
sentences.i: for this whole land was given as a kingdom to my grandfather David and, after him, to my father Solomon, and to me too after my father he has given it likewise, and I too shall subdue (?) you, like them. So now take counsel and obey me.’”
sentences.n: እስመ ኵላ ዘይእቲ ምድር ‘for the whole of this land’ (ኵላ + ዘይእቲ ‘this (f.)’); ተውህበት ‘it was given’, the passive of ወሀበ; መንግሥት ‘kingdom’. ለአበ አቡየ ‘to the father of my father’ is a construct chain. ወሊተኒ ‘and to me also’ (ሊተ ‘to me’ + -ኒ). The unit ends at ፨, which marks the end of the king’s speech in the text. ወይእዜኒ ‘and now also’; ምክሩ ‘take counsel’ and ተአዘዙ ‘obey’ (tä-stem of አዘዘ) are imperatives; ሊተ ‘me’. The entire speech is echoed from 1 Kings 12:14.

sentences.t: ወነገሮሙ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ለሊቃውንተ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: And-he-told-them thus to-the-chiefs-of Israel.
sentences.i: He spoke to the chiefs of Israel in this way.
sentences.n: ወነገሮሙ ‘he told them’; ከመዝ ‘thus’; ለሊቃውንተ is ለ- + ሊቃውንት ‘chiefs, masters’ (here a construct before እስራኤል). The narrative sums up: the speech was given as advised by the lads.

sentences.t: ወተንሥኡ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ኅቡረ ፡ በምልኦሙ ፡ ወይቤሉ ፡ እቱ ፡ ቤተከ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-they-arose all together in-their-fullness and-said: To-your-house (?), Israel;
sentences.i: They all rose together, in their full number, and said, “To your house (?), Israel!
sentences.n: ወተንሥኡ ‘and they arose’ (tä-stem of ንሥአ), ኵሎሙ ‘all of them’, ኅቡረ ‘together’ (adverbial accusative), በምልኦሙ ‘in their fullness’ (ምልኣት, with -ሙ). እቱ is unclear (?); I take it as a call to go, “to your house”, as in 1 Kings 12:16 (“To your tents, O Israel”), which has ‘tents’ where this has ‘house’. ቤተከ is ቤት ‘house’ (suffix stem ቤተ-, not a construct) + -ከ ‘your’ (sg.), the people addressing Israel.

sentences.t: አልብነኑ ፡ ዘናነግሥ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ በቤተ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ወበቤተ ፡ ብንያሚ ፤
sentences.l: is-there-not-for-us (?) who we-make-king except from-house-of Judah and-from-house-of Benjamin;
sentences.i: Have we no one to make king except from the house of Judah and the house of Benjamin?
sentences.n: አልብነኑ ‘is there not to us?’ (አልቦ ‘there is not’ + -ነ ‘to us’ + the question particle -ኑ). ዘናነግሥ ‘whom we shall make king’ (ዘ- + 1cp imperfect of አንገሠ). ዘእንበለ ‘except’; ወበቤተ ‘and from the house of’; ብንያሚ ‘Benjamin’; the two tribes that stayed with David’s line (1 Kings 12:21).

sentences.t: አበይናሆሙ ፡ ለቤቶሙ ፡ ወለሕዝበ ፡ ክልኤሆሙ ፡ ወናነግሥ ፡ ዘፈቀድነ ፡ ለርእስነ ፡ ወለዘሠምረት ፡ ነፍስነ ።
sentences.l: We-refused them, for-their-houses and-for-people-of both-of-them, and-we-will-make-king whom we-wished for-ourselves and-whom was-pleased our-soul.
sentences.i: We have refused them, their houses and the people of both of them, and we shall make king whomever we wish for ourselves, whomever our soul pleases.
sentences.n: አበይናሆሙ ‘we refused them’ (አበየ ‘refuse’ + -ሆሙ), ለቤቶሙ ‘their houses’, ወለሕዝበ ክልኤሆሙ ‘and the people of both of them’ (ክልኤ ‘two’ + -ሆሙ). ወናነግሥ ‘and we shall make king’; ዘፈቀድነ ‘whom we wished’ (ፈቀደ); ለዘሠምረት ነፍስነ ‘for him with whom our soul was pleased’ (ሠምረ ‘be pleased’, 3fs, because ነፍስ ‘soul’ is feminine).

sentences.t: ወጾሩ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ሐቅሎሙ ፡ ወጐዩ ፡ በምልኦሙ ፡ ወበጽሑ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሰማርያ ፡ ዘቤተ ፡ ኤፍራታ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-bore goods their-baggage (?) and-they-fled in-their-fullness and-arrived city Samaria of house-of Ephrata;
sentences.i: They loaded their goods and their baggage (?), fled in a body, and came to the city of Samaria, in the house of Ephrata;
sentences.n: ወጾሩ ‘and they carried’ (ጾረ ‘bear, load’); ንዋየ ‘goods, vessels’; ሐቅሎሙ ‘their baggage’ is a guess (?), from ሐቅል ‘lap, bosom’. ወጐዩ ‘they fled’ (ጐየ); ወበጽሑ ‘they arrived’ (በጽሐ + accusative of place). ሰማርያ is Samaria, the later capital of the north; ኤፍራታ ‘Ephrata’ stands for Ephraim’s territory, compare Ephrathah (Ruth 4:11, 1 Chronicles 4:4), here used as a tribal name for Ephraim (?).

sentences.t: ወበህየ ፡ መከሩ ፡ ወአንገለጉ ፡ ወተዓፀዉ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ከመ ፡ ያንግሡ ፡ ዘኀረዩ ፡ እምኔሆሙ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ረከቡ ፡ ዕፃ ፡ በውስተቤተ ፡ አቡሁ ፤
sentences.l: and-there they-took-counsel and-they-(?) and-they-cast-lots house-of Israel to-make-king him-who they-chose from-among-them for-him-on-whom they-found lot in-the-house-of his-father;
sentences.i: There they took counsel and deliberated (?), and the house of Israel cast lots to make king the one they had chosen from among them, the one for whom they found the lot in his father’s house;
sentences.n: ወበህየ ‘and there’; መከሩ ‘they took counsel’; ወአንገለጉ (?) is unclear, perhaps ‘they held back, considered’; ወተዓፀዉ ‘they cast lots’ (a tä-stem; the root ዐፀወ is my guess from ዕፃ ‘lot’ (?), compare Acts 1:26). ከመ ያንግሡ ‘that they make king’; ዘኀረዩ ‘whom they chose’ (ኀረየ); ለዘ ረከቡ ዕፃ ‘for him on whom they found the lot’, ዕፃ ‘lot’ (a different word, ዕፃ, from ዕፅ ‘wood’; the spelling is not consistent). The use of the lot for choosing a king recalls 1 Samuel 10:20–21 (Saul). በውስተቤተ is written as one word, በውስተ ‘in’ + ቤተ ‘house of’.

sentences.t: ወበጽሐ ፡ ዕፃ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ኤፍሬም ፡ ወልደ ፡ ናባጥ ፡ ወኀረዩ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወአንገሥዎ ፡ ለኢዮርብዓም ፤
sentences.l: and-arrived the-lot to the-house-of Ephraim son-of Nebat and-they-chose from-the-house of his-father and-they-made-king-him Jeroboam;
sentences.i: The lot came to the house of Ephraim, to the son of Nebat; they chose from his father’s house and made Jeroboam king;
sentences.n: ወበጽሐ ዕፃ ‘and the lot arrived’; ኀበ ‘to’; ኤፍሬም ‘Ephraim’ and ወልደ ናባጥ ‘son of Nebat’. Here ኢዮርብዓም is Jeroboam son of Nebat, of the tribe of Ephraim (1 Kings 11:26, 12:20); he shares the name with Solomon’s son, whom the text spells both ዮርብዓም and ኢዮርብዓም (ch. 69, and the genealogy below), so the spelling does not tell the two apart. ወአንገሥዎ ለኢዮርብዓም ‘they made king him, Jeroboam’ (አንገሠ + -ዎ, then the ለ- doubling the object).

sentences.t: ወከመዝ ፡ ተከፍለት ፡ መንግሥት ፡ እምኀበ ፡ ዮርብዓም ፡ ወልደ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወኢተርፎ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ብንያሚ ፡ ወቤተ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ አቡሁ ፨
sentences.l: and-thus it-was-divided the-kingdom from Jeroboam son-of Solomon and-there-did-not-remain except the-house-of Benjamin and-the-house-of Judah his-father ፨
sentences.i: And so the kingdom was divided from Jeroboam the son of Solomon, and nothing remained to him except the house of Benjamin and the house of Judah.
sentences.n: ወከመዝ ‘and thus’; ተከፍለት ‘it was divided’ (tä-stem of ከፈለ ‘divide’, 3fs, with መንግሥት ‘kingdom’ feminine); እምኀበ ‘from’ (here ‘from (the hand of)’). ወኢተርፎ ‘and there remained not to him’ (ተርፈ ‘remain’ + -ኦ). The word አቡሁ ‘his father’ at the end of the unit does not fit the grammar; I leave it untranslated and suspect an error or a displaced phrase (?). The unit ends at ፨, a larger break, and the next turns to scripture.

sentences.t: ወቃለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኢተሐሰ ፡ ወ ፡ ዘይቤሎ ፡ ለዳዊት ፡ ገብሩ ፡ እምፍሬ ፡ ከርሥከ ፡ ኣነብር ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበርከ ፤
sentences.l: And-the-word-of God was-not-shown-false (?), and what he-said to-David his-servant: Of-the-fruit-of your-belly I-will-set upon your-throne;
sentences.i: The word of God was not proved false, which he spoke to David his servant: “Of the fruit of your belly I shall set one upon your throne”;
sentences.n: ወቃለ እግዚኣብሔር ‘and the word of God’ (construct); ኢተሐሰ ‘was not proved false’, a tä-stem of ሐሰወ/ሐሰ ‘lie’ (?); the stray wordspace in ወ ፡ ዘይቤሎ is a printing or digitization oddity: it is ወዘይቤሎ ‘and which he said to him’ (?). ገብሩ ‘his servant’ in apposition. The quotation is Psalm 132:11 (131:11 in the Septuagint numbering): ‘Of the fruit of your belly I will set upon your throne’; ኣነብር is 1cs imperfect of አንበረ ‘set, place’, spelled with ኣ-. Compare 2 Samuel 7:12–16.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ሥሩዕ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወርኅ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said: Established like-the-moon for-ever;
sentences.i: Again he said, “It shall be established for ever like the moon”;
sentences.n: ወካዕበ ‘and again’; ሥሩዕ ‘established, ordered’ (passive participle of ሠርዐ); ወርኅ ‘moon, month’. Psalm 89:37 (88:38 in the Septuagint): ‘It shall be established for ever like the moon.’

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ መሐለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለዳዊት ፡ በጽድቅ ፡ ወኢይኔስሕ ።
sentences.l: And-again he-said: Swore God to-David in-truth and-not he-will-repent.
sentences.i: and again, “God swore to David in truth, and he will not repent.”
sentences.n: መሐለ ‘he swore’; ወኢይኔስሕ ‘and he will not repent’ (ነስሐ, with the negative ኢ-). Psalm 132:11 (131:11) and Psalm 110:4 (109:4) for the oath that God will not repent; compare Hebrews 7:21.

sentences.t: ዘነግሠ ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበረ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ዘመዱ ፡ በሥጋ ፡ እምድንግል ፡ ዘነበረ ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበረ ፡ መለኮቱ ፤
sentences.l: He-who-reigned upon throne-of David his-father is Jesus Christ, his-kinsman in-flesh from virgin, who sat upon throne-of his-divinity;
sentences.i: The one who reigned on the throne of his father David is Jesus Christ, his kinsman in the flesh, from a virgin, and who sits on the throne of his divinity;
sentences.n: ዘነግሠ ‘he who reigned’; the antecedent is ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ, and the answer to the promise of the psalms is that the true heir is Christ. ዘመዱ በሥጋ እምድንግል ‘his kinsman in the flesh, from a virgin’ (ዘመድ ‘kinsman, kin’ + -ሁ; the ዘ is part of the noun, not a relative); the descent from David through Mary (Luke 1:32–33). ዘነበረ ‘who sat’ (the perfect, here with the sense of the permanent state); መለኮቱ ‘his divinity’ (መለኮት + -ሁ). The Zion/Ark theology of the book treats the earthly kingdom as the shadow of the heavenly.

sentences.t: ወበምድርኒ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ ዘይነግሥ ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበሩ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ በኵሩ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፤
sentences.l: And-on-earth-also he-gave the-one-who he-reigns upon his-throne king-of Ethiopia, his-firstborn to-Solomon;
sentences.i: And on earth too he gave one who reigns on his throne, the king of Ethiopia, the firstborn of Solomon;
sentences.n: ወበምድርኒ ‘and on earth also’ (ምድር + -ኒ); ወሀቦ ‘he gave him’ (ወሀበ + -ኦ); ዘይነግሥ ‘who reigns’. ንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያ ‘king of Ethiopia’ is in apposition; በኵሩ ለሰሎሞን ‘firstborn to Solomon’ is Menelik (ምኒልክ), son of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, the dynasty’s ancestor, who in this book is the heir of David’s throne on earth.

sentences.t: ወለዮርበዓምሰ ፡ ኢወሀቦ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ፪ ፡ በትር ፤
sentences.l: and-to-Jeroboam-indeed he-did-not-give God except two rods;
sentences.i: but to Jeroboam God gave only two tribes;
sentences.n: ወለዮርበዓምሰ ‘and as for Jeroboam’ (here spelled ዮርበዓም, with ለ- + the contrastive -ሰ). ኢወሀቦ ‘he did not give him’; ዘእንበለ ‘except’; ፪ is the numeral 2 (spoken ክልኤቱ, kəlʾetu); በትር ‘rod, staff’ is used for ‘tribe’ (compare Hebrew shevet). The two are Judah and Benjamin (1 Kings 12:20–21).

sentences.t: ወንጉሠሮምሂ ፡ ወልዱ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ዘይንእስ ።
sentences.l: and-king-of Rome-also his-son to-Solomon who is-younger.
sentences.i: The king of Rome too is a son of Solomon, the younger one.
sentences.n: ወንጉሠሮምሂ is written as one word: ወ- ‘and’ + ንጉሠ ‘king of’ (construct) + ሮም ‘Rome’ + -ሂ ‘also’, ‘and the king of Rome too’, as in ch. 17–20 where Rome and Ethiopia are the two kingdoms of Solomon’s sons. ወልዱ ለሰሎሞን ‘his son, Solomon’s’ (ለ- naming the father); ዘይንእስ ‘who is young, the younger’ (ንእሰ ‘be small, young’), set beside the firstborn of the previous unit but one.

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ ዘገብረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይበሉነ ፡ አብዳን ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወበእንተ ፡ ዮርብዓም ፡ ወልዱ ፡ እስመ ፡ ማእምረ ፡ ልብ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያምስሉ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ገብረ ።
sentences.l: And-this that did God so-that-not they-call-us fools people-of Jews concerning Solomon and-concerning Jeroboam his-son, for knower-of heart God, so-that not they-liken that this he-did.
sentences.i: God did this so that the Jewish people would not call us fools on account of Solomon and his son Jeroboam; for God knows the heart, lest they suppose that he did this (?).
sentences.n: ወዘንተ ዘገብረ እግዚኣብሔር ‘and this which God did’; ከመ ኢይበሉነ ‘that they not call us’ (the subjunctive with ኢ-, and -ነ ‘us’); አብዳን ‘fools’ (plural of አብድ); ሕዝበ አይሁድ ‘people of the Jews’ (construct). The speaker identifies with the Solomonic line of Ethiopia against the Jewish claim. ማእምረ ልብ ‘knower of the heart’ (ማእምር + construct ልብ). The last clause (ከመ ኢያምስሉ ዘንተ ገብረ) is uncertain (?): ‘lest they suppose that he (God, or Solomon) did this’, or ‘lest they make him like’; the subject of ገብረ is left open. Compare Acts 1:24 and 1 Samuel 16:7.

sentences.t: ወለዮርብዓምኒ ፡ ሰመይዎ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ወለንጉሠ ፡ ሰማርያ ፡ ሰመይዎ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: And-Jeroboam-also they-called king-of Judah, and-the-king-of Samaria they-called king-of Israel.
sentences.i: They called Jeroboam too king of Judah, and they called the king of Samaria king of Israel.
sentences.n: ወለዮርብዓምኒ ‘and Jeroboam also’; ሰመይዎ ‘they called him’ (ሰመየ ‘name, call’ + -ዎ). ለንጉሠ ሰማርያ ‘the king of Samaria’ with ለ- doubling the object. The northern kingdom took the name Israel, the southern Judah. The text gives the two kings the same name, Solomon’s son (here ዮርብዓም) and the Ephraimite (ኢዮርብዓም above).

sentences.t: ወእምትውልደ ፡ ኢዮርብዓም ፡ ኮነት ፡ ትውልድ ፡ እስከ ፡ ኢያቄም ፡ ፵ወ፩ ፡ ወአሜሃ ፡ ተወልዱ ፡ ለመልኪ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ ደቂቅ ፡ ሌዊ ፡ ወሴም ፡ ወላዴ ፡ ሆናሴ ፤
sentences.l: And-from-the-descent-of Jeroboam was the-generation until Joachim, 41, and-then they-were-born to-Melki two sons Levi and-Shem and-the-father-of Honase;
sentences.i: From the descendants of Jeroboam the generations ran down to Joachim, forty-one in all; and then two sons were born to Melki, Levi and Shem, the father of Honase (?);
sentences.n: ወእምትውልደ ‘and from the descent of’ (ትውልድ ‘generation’); ኮነት ትውልድ ‘there was a generation’; እስከ ‘until’. ኢያቄም is Joachim, father of Mary in the tradition (the Protevangelium of James); the text counts forty-one generations from Solomon’s son (ኢዮርብዓም here, Rehoboam in the heading) to him, in the numeral ፵ወ፩ (spoken አርብዓ ወአሐዱ, arbəʿa wä-ʾähadu, ‘forty-one’). ወአሜሃ ‘and then’. ተወልዱ ‘they were born’; ለመልኪ ‘to Melki’ (a name, Melchi in Luke 3:24); ክልኤ ‘two’ (the short form of ክልኤቱ before a noun) with the plural ደቂቅ ‘sons’. ወላዴ ሆናሴ ‘and begetter of Honase’ (ወላዲ ‘begetter’, construct); the names correspond loosely to Luke’s genealogy. The names and sequence differ from the Gospels, and my reading of the apposition is uncertain (?).

sentences.t: ወሆናሴ ፡ ወለደ ፡ ቀላምዮስ ፡ ወቀላምዮስ ፡ ወለደ ፡ ኢየቄ ፡ ም ፡ ወኢያቄምኒ ፡ ወለዳ ፡ ለማርያም ፡ ወለተ ፡ ዳዊት ፤
sentences.l: And-Honase begot Qalamyos, and-Qalamyos begot Iyeqe-m, and-Joachim begot Mary daughter-of David;
sentences.i: Honase begot Qalamyos, Qalamyos begot Joachim, and Joachim begot Mary, a daughter of David;
sentences.n: ወለደ ‘he begot’. The name ኢየቄ ፡ ም is split by a wordspace in the source, a printing or copying error for ኢያቄም ‘Joachim’ (?); ወኢያቄምኒ ‘and Joachim also’. ወለዳ ‘he begot her’; ለማርያም ‘Mary’, the object with ለ-; ወለተ ዳዊት ‘daughter of David’, an accusative construct, so Mary comes from David’s line. The genealogy is a tradition not found in the Gospels, which gives Joseph’s line in Matthew 1 and Luke 3.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ኢሊ ፡ ወለደ ፡ መልኪ ፡ ወሜልኪ ፡ ወለዶ ፡ ለማቲ ፡ ወማቴ ፡ ወለዶሙ ፡ ለኤሊ ፡ ወለያዕቆብ ፡ ወለሐና ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ ኢያቄም ፤
sentences.l: And-again Eli begot Melki, and-Melki begot Mati, and-Mate begot Eli and-Jacob and-Hanna wife-of Joachim;
sentences.i: And again, Eli begot Melki, and Melki begot Mati, and Mati begot Eli, Jacob, and Hanna, the wife of Joachim;
sentences.n: ወካዕበ ‘and again’. A second chain of names, ኢሊ, ሜልኪ, ማቲ (ማቴ), ኤሊ, ያዕቆብ, and ሐና ‘Hanna’, wife of Joachim, thus Mary’s mother and Jacob’s sister. ወለዶ ‘he begot him’, ወለዶሙ ‘he begot them’: -ኦ and -ሙ as object suffixes. The names Eli and Jacob are those of Joseph’s fathers in Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16.

sentences.t: ወአውሰበ ፡ ኤሊ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ ወሞተ ፡ እንዘ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ውሉደ ፡ ወአውሰባ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ለብእሲተ ፡ ኤሊ ፡ ዮሐዳ ፡ ወወለደ ፡ ላቲ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ ጸራቤ ፡ ዘፈኀራ ፡ ለማርያም ።
sentences.l: And-Eli took-a-wife and-died while there-is-not children, and-Jacob took-her, the-wife-of Eli, Yohada, and-begot by-her Joseph, carpenter, who betrothed Mary.
sentences.i: Eli took a wife and died without children, and Jacob took Eli’s wife Yohada and begot by her Joseph the carpenter, who betrothed Mary (?).
sentences.n: ወአውሰበ ‘he took a wife’ (አውሰበ ‘marry’); እንዘ አልቦ ውሉደ ‘while there were no children’. ወአውሰባ ‘he took her to wife’ is the levirate marriage (Deuteronomy 25:5–6): Jacob marries his dead brother’s widow, and the son Joseph is legally Eli’s. ዮሐዳ ‘Yohada’ names the widow (?). ጸራቤ ‘carpenter’ (ጸራቢ); ዘፈኀራ ለማርያም ‘who betrothed Mary’: ዘ- + ፈኀረ (3ms perfect, active) + -ኣ ‘her’, with ለማርያም restating the object; the verb I cannot confirm and ‘betrothed’ is from the context (?), so the passive of the Gospels is not what the form says. The reconciling of Matthew 1:16 (Jacob) and Luke 3:23 (Eli) by levirate marriage is an old explanation (Julius Africanus).

sentences.t: ወዮሴፍሰ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ በሥጋወወልደኤሊ ፡ በሕገ ፡ ኦሪት ፡ በከመ ፡ አዘዞ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይትዋሰቡ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዘመዶሙ ፡ በበ ፡ አብያተ ፡ አበዊሆሙ ፡ ወኢይትዋሰቡ ፡ እምባዕድ ፡ ዘመድ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-Joseph-indeed son-of Jacob in-flesh and-son-of Eli by-the-law-of Torah, as he-commanded-him God to-Moses so-that they-marry each-other with their-kin each-according-to the-houses-of their-fathers and-not they-marry from foreign kin ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: Joseph was the son of Jacob by flesh and the son of Eli by the Law of the Torah, as God commanded Moses that they should marry among their own kin, each within the houses of their fathers, and not marry from a foreign kin.
sentences.n: ወዮሴፍሰ ‘and Joseph indeed’; ወልደ ‘son of’ (construct). The text writes በሥጋወወልደኤሊ without word division for በሥጋ ወወልደ ኤሊ ‘in flesh and son of Eli’ (the source text joins them). በሕገ ኦሪት ‘by the law of the Torah’; በከመ አዘዞ ‘as he commanded him’; ይትዋሰቡ ‘they marry one another’ (tä-stem of ወሰበ); ምስለ ዘመዶሙ ‘with their kin’; በበ አብያተ አበዊሆሙ ‘each by the houses of their fathers’, which alludes to Numbers 36:6–9, the rule that heiresses marry within their tribe. ኢይትዋሰቡ እምባዕድ ዘመድ ‘they shall not intermarry from a foreign kin’. The row ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ marks the end of the chapter and stays with the last unit.
